correctness.rationale: The impulse kernel is exactly the Green-function convolution of three-dimensional diffusion with constant linear loss. Its logarithmic derivative has one zero, giving a single post-pulse peak, and equality of impulse terms leads without approximation to equation (1). Setting z=a/(p*delta) gives z-log z=B+E(z), where 0<E(z)<=2a/(pT) uniformly for all k>=0. Inverting the monotone scalar function proves the stated B+log B+O(log B/B+a/T) asymptotic. A standard-library script checks test values, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The concentration peak after cessation of extracellular iontophoresis is a motivated and experimentally monitored quantity. The exact asymptotic determines a sharp transition between logarithmically slow post-pulse lag in nearly conservative diffusion and inverse-duration lag under fixed first-order removal. Its error bound uniform for arbitrary joint scaling of uptake and release length makes the threshold more than a fixed-parameter Taylor expansion, and does not require a separate large-T simulation at each uptake rate.
